chapters.title: One ship, one contract
chapters.text: You sign the founding papers with one ship, a little borrowed credit, and a route between Aurum Station and Verdant Reach. Nobody out here needs a hero, only someone who notices what a world is short of and has room in the hold.

chapters.title: The first ledger line
chapters.text: The ore goes down the ramp at Verdant Reach and the credits arrive before the ship has finished cooling. It is a small number, but it is the first line in a ledger that did not exist this morning, and you read it twice.

chapters.title: Hands off the wheel
chapters.text: You set a ship on its route and step away from the console. It docks, unloads, and turns for home with nobody watching, and you spend the whole trip hovering in case it is a mistake. It is not.

chapters.title: Faster engines
chapters.text: The refit crews bolt new drives onto the hull and the trips get noticeably shorter. Contracts that used to leave a gap in the schedule now close with time to spare.

chapters.title: Bigger holds
chapters.text: The hauler refit doubles as a lesson in why colonies always seem to want a little more than one hold carries. Now a single trip covers a whole order, and the dock crews stop giving you sympathetic looks.

chapters.title: Another pair of hands
chapters.text: Research opens another slot for a self-running ship, and you realise the fleet is no longer limited by how many routes you can keep in your head. It is limited by how many you are willing to trust.

chapters.title: Whichever is most urgent
chapters.text: You tell the fleet to look for whichever colony is running lowest and head there. It feels like handing the map to someone else, right up until the first shortfall is filled before you have even noticed it.

chapters.title: Changing course
chapters.text: An idle ship turns away from its usual dock and heads for a colony that needs it more. Nobody told it to. You note the new route in the ledger with something close to pride.

chapters.title: Every slot running
chapters.text: Every automation slot is filled, and the console is oddly quiet. The work has not gone away; it has moved from moving cargo to deciding what the fleet should be for.

chapters.title: Growing pains
chapters.text: A colony you have been supplying steadily reaches its next level of development, and its needs grow with it. The dock manager sends a polite message that amounts to: more, please, and a wider range this time.

chapters.title: A little of everything
chapters.text: You have now sold every good the home system makes. The market boards used to show only your favourites; now the whole system's prices are a map you can read at a glance.

chapters.title: A modest fortune
chapters.text: The total on the ledger passes ten thousand credits. It would not buy a colony, but it would buy a very comfortable retirement on one, and you find you have no interest in that at all.

chapters.title: Let it recover
chapters.text: You flooded one market and watched its price sink, then routed your ships elsewhere and gave it time. The price crept back up on its own, and you remember it: markets forgive, if you let them.

chapters.title: An established economy
chapters.text: All five home-system colonies have grown into themselves, each leaning on the others in its own way. Aurum, Verdant, Ferrum, Cryo, Helion: the routes between them now look less like a plan and more like a habit.

chapters.title: The Guild's first contract
chapters.text: A message from the Trade Guild arrives asking for a bulk delivery to a colony that needs it. You deliver, they pay a bonus on top of the sale, and the Guild sends a short note of thanks that reads as if written by a person who has seen many late shipments.

chapters.title: Fully studied
chapters.text: The last shared research node is done, and one specialization path stands finished. The research board is at last a list of things you know rather than things you might, and you take a moment to enjoy how ordinary it feels.

chapters.title: The Kepler Cluster
chapters.text: The expansion charter clears and the map opens outward to the Kepler Cluster: Alpha, Beta and Gamma, three new worlds that need each other as much as your first five did. The first ship out carries more hope than cargo.

chapters.title: Frontier boomtown
chapters.text: A Kepler colony reaches its second level of development, well past the range of any old home-system schedule. The frontier is not a place you visit and leave; it is a place that has started to pay its own way.

chapters.title: A name the Guild knows
chapters.text: Five Guild contracts delivered, and the dispatcher now greets your ships by name. Nothing formal changes, but you notice the offers now feel less like requests to a stranger and more like errands between colleagues.

chapters.title: A trading dynasty
chapters.text: One hundred thousand credits of profit, counted line by line across every route you ever ran. You go back through the early pages of the ledger and find the first sale, and it looks very small and very brave.

chapters.title: Past the Rift
chapters.text: The Outer Reaches research clears and the charts show the Rift Colonies, three worlds trading crystal, antimatter and polymer among themselves. They are further out than anything you have supplied, and their needs are stranger, but the logic of the routes is the same.

chapters.title: The Umbral Deep
chapters.text: Beyond the Rift the map goes dark and quiet: Nadir Foundry, Hush Cryostat and Tenebra Loom, far from any sun and paying the best prices anywhere. It is the furthest anyone has traded, and the ledger has never had lines this long.

chapters.title: A galaxy at scale
chapters.text: The fleet runs itself, the colonies feed one another, and you find yourself checking in on the whole thing the way you would check on a garden. It works. You are, for the first time, not needed on every trip.

chapters.title: A new beginning
chapters.text: You close the books on the old company and found a new one, keeping only a legacy behind you: a little more starting capital and a slightly better name on every sale. One ship, one route, and this time you know how it goes.

chapters.title: A line in the charter
chapters.text: Renewing the charter earns charter points, and you spend the first of them on something small and permanent: one line written into every charter to come. It is not much. It is yours, and it will still be there when the world resets.

chapters.title: Three charters deep
chapters.text: Three times now you have closed the books at the top of the galaxy and opened them again at the bottom. The clerks stop asking questions. Each opening is a little different, and each time you know a little better where the first bottleneck will be.

chapters.title: Against the grain
chapters.text: You chose the harder charter: prices that sag faster, colonies that ask for more sooner. And you still carried it to the end. Nobody hands out a medal for that, but the ledger remembers, and so do you.

chapters.title: A name on the manifest
chapters.text: One of your haulers has flown the same lane so many times it could do it asleep, and the crew says it deserves a captain. You open the roster, read four very different résumés, and pick one. The ship's log gains a name, and the crew gains an opinion about everything.

chapters.title: The whole roster
chapters.text: Frugal, lucky, nocturnal and exacting: you have now put each of the four captains in a seat at least once. They trade stories at every dock, mostly about each other, and every one of them swears the others are exaggerating.

chapters.title: A thousand quiet ledgers
chapters.text: Beyond the routes you fly yourself, a whole background galaxy of worlds has grown to its full size, each one sending a small, steady trickle of revenue your way. You will never visit most of them, but every one of them is, quietly, part of the company.

chapters.title: The lights stay off
chapters.text: You ran the whole charter with the map dark and the prices shown as ranges, buying back each piece of information only when it earned its keep. At the end the ledger gets a small stamp, a half-moon with the words dark run beside it. The ledger does not say whether it was harder; it only notes that you did not look.

chapters.title: Reading the sky
chapters.text: Five times the dock gossip turned out to be right: a festival here, a strike there, a few days of prices bending around it. You start to read the weather the way a farmer reads a sky, and to buy the grain a day before everyone else decides they want it.

chapters.title: The long way round
chapters.text: One ship goes the long way round, away from every route you have ever scheduled, and comes home a dozen ticks later with a story it is not quite able to tell. The ledger notes the missing income and, beside it, a small line that says only: worth knowing.

chapters.title: A cabinet of small odd things
chapters.text: Twelve small things now sit in the cabinet on the office wall: a polite beacon, a patient clock, a chipped moon. None of them is worth a credit and nobody can explain why you would not sell the lot for the shelf space.
